newsitem.title: USA: Cleveland schools paid too much to borrow -- paper.
newsitem.headline: Cleveland schools paid too much to borrow -- paper.

text.p: The financially strapped Cleveland schools paid nearly $2.5 million too much to borrow in the period leading up to the state takeover of the district in 1995, the Cleveland Plain Dealer reported Sunday.

By failing to obtain insurance or letters of credit when issuing debt from 1992 until the takeover, the schools paid nearly $1.8 million in excessive interest, the newspaper reported in the first article of a three-part series.
The remainder of the excess costs came in failing to negotiate a competitive interest rate with underwriter McDonald & Co Securities Inc. in a 1993 deal, the newspaper reported.
In the article, McDonald defended its work, and said the rate comparisons to other deals the newspaper made were unfair because of Cleveland's unique credit situation at the time of the deals.

Under state control, the district has moved to competitive bidding, greatly reducing its costs in two deals since the takeover, the Plain Dealer reported. The district expects to issue nearly $150 million of securities in the next few weeks, district Treasurer Bryan Christman told the Plain Dealer.

McDonald and Calfee Halter, the district's bond counsel for seven consecutive issues, contributed about $30,000 to a levy referendum in 1994, the Plain Dealer reported. Employees of McDonald and Calfee Halter also contributed to the "reform" slate of candidates that ran the district in the period and Mayor Michael White's campaign funds, the newspaper reported.

After recommending McDonald as underwriter on three consecutive deals, former schools Treasurer Paul Yacobian retired from the district in July 1992 and joined the investment banking firm two months later, the Plain Dealer reported.
On Monday, the Plain Dealer reported that a firm headed by a financial adviser to the district, Charles E. Brown, had borrowed money from McDonald beginning in April 1993.

Chase Global Securities Inc. served as adviser to securities deals in June 1993 and March 1994 in which McDonald also participated, the Plain Dealer reported. Even after their relationship was disclosed to former school Treasurer William Aldridge later in 1994, he recommended both firms be hired for a December 1994 debt issuance and a 1995 deal never completed because of the state takeover, the newspaper reported.
The relationship between Chase Global and McDonald was not disclosed in the official statement to potential bond buyers, the Plain Dealer reported.
McDonald said its campaign contributions were proper.
